methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $10.35B (to $29.03B) × margin 8.0% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $7.39B
K = capital to build it: $10.35B ÷ sales-to-capital 3.17 = $3.27B
σ = 37% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $5.00B
assets in place = NOPAT $0 ÷ WACC = $0; value = ($0 + $5.00B − net debt $1.80B) ÷ 37,142,257 = $86.24
inputs: SEC 10-K / 10-Q, trailing four quarters (the main site's reading of the filings)

Return on new capital in perpetuity
methods.fit: It is loss-making or growing fast: much of its value is the chance to become a larger, profitable business, which behaves like an option — worth more the more uncertain it is.

methods.formula: Value = D₀ × [(1 + g_L) + H × (g_S − g_L)] ÷ (kₑ − g_L);  growth falls in a straight line from g_S to g_L over 2H years
